newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FULL TEXT-RBA waiting for wages - Macfarlane.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FULL TEXT-RBA waiting for wages - Macfarlane.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Ian Macfarlane made some comments about the economy and monetary policy in answer to a question after an address to the Sydney Institute on Tuesday evening.
Macfarlane was asked if the Reserve Bank could do more to reduce unemployment over the next year or so, given the good inflation outlook.
A full text of his reply follows.
"The considerations that you have to take into account when you do this are you make a policy now for what you think the events will be in a year's time.
"You may not be able to accurately forecast (a year out). Maybe you put more weight on what you see coming in six months time or in eighteen months time, but that's what you're trying to do.
"That's why we had three easings in monetary policy in the second half of 1996 and we're looking with some interest to see how the effects of those are coming through.

"The current feeling is that some of the effects are coming through. Our feeling is that the sort of information that we have received over the last couple of months is better than the sort of information we were receiving during the second half of
1996 when we were making those (interest rate) easings and I refer specifically to investment and also I think to a turnaround in the housing sector.
"And of course in employment, where the growth in employment in the last two quarters of last year was a bit higher than what they were a bit earlier in the year.
"If you take all these things into account then you form a view of how the economy is going to grow through the course of 1997 and what you think is going to happen to inflation.

"And you're right, the near term outlook for inflation is very good and we think the 1997 outlook for economic activity is also good -- stronger through 1997 than it was through 1996. "We also have to take into account not just the near term outlook for inflation, we take into account something stretching a bit a longer than a year or 18 months.

"When we do that of course developments on the wages front form an important part of that. So if you have some important information on this, either from the market sector or the administered sector then it would be only logical to wait until you saw what the results were."
